defaultRequirement: Build a Slack connector that supports creating, reading, updating, and deleting messages.
summary: Slack supports all four message operations, but update and delete are limited by who wrote the message and which token the connector uses. Confirm the client's deletion expectations before building.

capabilities.label: Create messages
capabilities.conditions: Needs the chat:write scope. The app must be a member of the channel, or also hold chat:write.public to post in public channels it has not joined.

capabilities.label: Read messages
capabilities.conditions: Needs history scopes per conversation type (channels:history, groups:history, im:history, mpim:history). Since 2025, apps distributed outside the Slack Marketplace are limited to 1 request per minute and 15 messages per request on these methods. Internal (customer-built) apps keep higher limits.

evidence.title: Rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps (changelog, May 2025)

capabilities.label: Update messages
capabilities.conditions: Bot tokens can only edit messages posted by that bot. User tokens can only edit messages that user could edit in Slack.

evidence.title: chat.update reference (ownership rule assumed to match chat.delete; re-check before quoting to a client)

capabilities.label: Delete messages
capabilities.conditions: Depends on whose messages must be deleted. Answer the question above to resolve this.

evidence.title: chat.delete: bot tokens may delete only messages posted by that bot; user tokens only messages that user can delete
Modifying messages guide: a Workspace Admin's user token can delete most messages

clarifications.question: Whose messages must the connector be able to delete?
clarifications.why: Slack enforces different deletion rules for bot tokens, user tokens and admin user tokens. The answer changes the auth design and whether the requirement can be met at all.

options.label: Only messages the connector itself posted

effects.conditions: A bot token with chat:write can delete messages that bot posted. No extra approval needed.

options.label: Messages written by the person who connected Slack

effects.conditions: Needs a user token (user scope chat:write) for each person. It can delete only what that person can delete in Slack, and workspace settings may stop members deleting their own messages.

Only possible with the user token of a Workspace Admin or Owner. A bot token cannot do this. Expect security review from the client, and confirm this is really the business need. Retention policies may be a better fit.

options.label: Permanently erase messages, including from exports and compliance holds

effects.conditions: chat.delete removes the message from the conversation, but the docs checked do not say how it interacts with exports, legal holds or Enterprise retention. Escalate to Slack support with the client's exact compliance requirement.

auth.recommended: OAuth 2.0 (Slack 'OAuth v2') installing a bot token (xoxb-)
auth.why: Bot tokens survive when the installing person leaves, and they are enough for create, read and editing the bot's own messages.
alternatives: Add a user token (xoxp-) only if the connector must act on messages written by people.
Optional token rotation gives expiring tokens plus a refresh token. Turn it on for long-lived production installs.

blockers.title: Workspace may require admin approval to install apps
blockers.detail: Many workspaces restrict app installation. Someone with install rights must approve the app and its scopes.
blockers.resolution: Send the prepared approval request listing scopes and why each is needed.
blockers.handoff: Hi! We're building a Slack integration for {requirement}. It needs these scopes: chat:write, channels:history, groups:history. Could you approve the app install (or tell us your app approval process)? Docs: https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/installing-with-oauth

blockers.title: Workspace Admin must connect their own account
blockers.detail: Deleting any message requires a Workspace Admin or Owner's user token. The connector acts with their full permissions, so most security teams will want to review it.
blockers.resolution: Confirm the business need first (retention settings may solve it), then send the prepared request.
blockers.handoff: Hi! The client asked for a connector that can delete any message in the workspace ({requirement}). Slack only allows this with a Workspace Admin/Owner user token (chat.delete docs: https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.delete). Could you (1) confirm this is required rather than a retention policy, and (2) if yes, be the admin who authorizes the app?

blockers.title: Low message-history rate limit for distributed non-Marketplace apps
blockers.detail: If the app is installed in other organizations' workspaces without being on the Slack Marketplace, conversations.history is limited to 1 request/minute and 15 messages per request.
blockers.resolution: Decide early: build as an internal app per workspace, apply for the Slack Marketplace, or design reads around webhooks/Events API instead of history polling.

blockers.title: Slack Marketplace review if listing publicly
blockers.detail: Listing on the Marketplace is optional but requires Slack's review. Review time is not published.
blockers.resolution: Prepare listing materials in parallel with development. Treat review time as unknown in plans.

alternatives.insteadOf: Deleting any message in the workspace
alternatives.option: Connector deletes only its own messages, and the client uses Slack's retention settings for everything else
alternatives.doesNotCover: Targeted deletion of individual human-authored messages on demand

alternatives.option: Subscribe to message events with the Events API
alternatives.doesNotCover: Backfilling history from before the app was installed

engineering.assumptions: Bot-token install, standard OAuth, one workspace for testing.

waiting.notes: None for your own workspace. Client workspace approval: hours to days. Marketplace review: unknown.

uncertainty: Final deletion semantics depend on the client's answer above
Rate limits depend on how the app is distributed

tasks.title: Get a Slack workspace where you can install apps
tasks.detail: A free workspace you own is fine for testing.
tasks.doneWhen: You can open https://api.slack.com/apps and click 'Create New App'.

tasks.title: Decide bot token vs. bot + user token
tasks.detail: Use the answer to 'Whose messages must the connector delete?'. Only add user scopes if you need to act on people's messages.
tasks.doneWhen: Scope list is written down and agreed with the client.

tasks.title: Create the app and add bot scopes
tasks.detail: In 'OAuth & Permissions', add chat:write, channels:history (and groups:history / im:history if needed).

tasks.title: Add your redirect URL
tasks.detail: Must exactly match the callback URL in your connector.

tasks.title: Implement the OAuth v2 flow
tasks.detail: Send users to the authorize URL, then exchange the code at oauth.v2.access. Store the bot token encrypted.
tasks.doneWhen: Your app stores an xoxb- token after installing.

tasks.title: Wire up the four operations
tasks.detail: chat.postMessage, conversations.history, chat.update, chat.delete. Keep the 'ts' value of each message. Update and delete both need it.
tasks.doneWhen: Each operation is callable from your connector.

tasks.title: Run the ownership test
tasks.detail: Post as the bot, then update and delete it (should succeed). Then try deleting a human's message with the bot token. Expect 'cant_delete_message'. This proves the restriction rather than assuming it.
tasks.doneWhen: Results recorded in the Evidence tab.

tasks.title: Decide distribution and rate-limit strategy
tasks.detail: Internal app vs. distributed vs. Marketplace. See the rate-limit blocker.

tasks.title: Turn on token rotation and handle 'token_revoked'
tasks.detail: Ask users to reconnect when tokens are revoked.
